One thing I genuinely enjoy about software development is taking an idea and turning it into something people can actually use. 

That's what I set out to do with Nath ResellDesk.

ResellDesk is a ticket reseller management application I built to make everyday business activities easier. It helps users manage ticket inventory, record sales, monitor revenue and profit, track events, and receive notifications.

Building this project involved more than writing code. I worked on the interface, authentication, browser-based data storage, serverless functions, email delivery, notification integrations, deployment, and debugging.

Here is the actual technology stack behind ResellDesk:

🔹 Frontend

- HTML5
- CSS3 (CSS Variables, Grid, Flexbox and Media Queries)
- Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules)
- Google Fonts (DM Sans and Plus Jakarta Sans)
- Browser APIs (IndexedDB, localStorage, Fetch API and HTML Dialog)

🔹 Authentication

- Supabase Auth
- supabase-js 2.45.4

🔹 Data Storage

- IndexedDB (ResellDeskDB) for locally storing tickets and sales records in each user's browser
- localStorage for saving theme preferences

🔹 Backend and Notifications

- Netlify Functions
- Node.js
- esbuild
- Resend for email delivery
- Telegram Bot API
- Discord Webhooks

🔹 Hosting and Deployment

- Netlify
- GitHub
- Netlify Environment Variables
- Automatic deployment from GitHub

🔹 Development Tools

- Visual Studio Code
- Git
- GitHub
- Netlify CLI
- "netlify dev" for local development and testing

A few technical details worth mentioning:

ResellDesk uses Vanilla JavaScript. There is no React, no frontend framework and no build step.

Supabase handles authentication, while IndexedDB stores ticket and sales records locally in each user's browser. Cloud synchronisation is not currently implemented.

Netlify hosts the application and serverless notification function, while Resend handles email delivery through a verified domain. Telegram and Discord are used for administrator alerts.

I'm sharing this project because I want people to see not just the finished application, but also the technologies, engineering decisions and practical development skills behind it.

I'm constantly learning, building and improving my craft as a Full-Stack Software Engineer.

💸📉 YOUR “FAIR” PRICE MIGHT BE KILLING YOUR GROWTH
 
One Price for Everyone? That’s the Fastest Way to Lose Customers
 
Category: FINANCIAL WISDOM
 
I’ve watched entrepreneurs leave thousands of dollars on the table — for one simple reason.
 
They assumed every customer, in every country, values money the same way.
 
They don’t.
 
A price that feels “cheap” in New York can feel impossible in Lagos. A price that feels “premium” in London might actually reduce trust in Jakarta.
 
That’s the quiet truth most founders miss — and it’s costing you growth.
 
💡 Pricing isn’t math. It’s emotion, timing, and local reality.
 
Right now, pressure is everywhere. Acquisition costs are up. Demand is shifting. Investors are pushing for faster revenue. So founders react — they slash prices globally… or force one number onto the whole world.
 
Both are dangerous.
 
Ignoring local purchasing power is like building a skyscraper on sand. It looks solid — until the foundation shifts. ⚠️
 
💡 I consulted a SaaS founder who learned this the hard way. He launched globally at $19/$29/$49. Traffic was strong. Interest was high. But conversions in emerging markets? Almost zero.
 
Instead of spending more on ads, he changed one thing. He tested regional pricing.
 
💰 Wealthy markets → kept premium.
🌍 Emerging markets → $3/$7/$12 tiers.
 
The result? Revenue increased across every region. The mid-tier option became the bestseller everywhere. Customers finally felt the price matched their reality.
 
Data from ProfitWell backs this up — smart regional pricing can lift conversions by nearly 30%.
 
🧠 The entrepreneurs winning globally aren’t always cheaper. They’re simply more relevant.
 
 
 
✅ ACTIONABLE STEPS 
 
1️⃣ Map purchasing power before setting global pricing.

2️⃣ Test at least 3 price points within 30 days.

3️⃣ Track conversions per country — never average them.

4️⃣ Build a strong mid-tier — most people avoid extremes.

5️⃣ Ask local users directly: “Does this feel fair to you?”

6️⃣ Chase sustainable profit — not vanity revenue screenshots.
 
 
 
📊 POLL 

Which pricing mistake hurts you most?
 
🔘 One global price for everyone
🔘 Pricing too low out of fear
🔘 Ignoring local psychology
🔘 Copying competitors blindly
 
 
 
🚨 COMMON MYSTAKES

⚠️ You’re pricing globally because others do it — not because your customers need it.
 
⚠️ Too-low pricing can destroy trust faster than high pricing.
 
⚠️ If your pricing is based on assumptions instead of testing — cash burn is inevitable.
 
The bottom line: Sustainable growth doesn’t come from charging everyone the same. It comes from understanding how different people experience value. 

Adapt without losing profitability. That’s the sweet spot — and it’s where the winners play.
 
✍️ Is your pricing global or local? Has a price change ever unlocked massive growth? Let’s discuss in the comments — I’d love to hear your story.

🚗 THE AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY DOESN'T NEED ANOTHER GREEN MATERIAL.
IT NEEDS A MATERIAL THAT PASSES THE TEST.

For automotive manufacturers, choosing a material is not simply about where it comes from. It is about how it performs inside a component.
Mechanical properties. Thermal behavior. Moisture resistance. Durability. Processability. Batch consistency. Every requirement matters.

🥥 THIS IS WHERE COCOFIBER ENTERS THE MATERIAL-ENGINEERING CONVERSATION.
Researchers have investigated coir-fiber-reinforced polypropylene composites for potential automotive applications.

But there is an important distinction:
RAW COCOFIBER IS NOT AN AUTOMOTIVE COMPONENT. IT IS A POTENTIAL REINFORCEMENT MATERIAL.
Its performance depends on much more than the fiber itself.

Several factors influence the final composite:
📏 Fiber length and geometry — influence reinforcement behavior.
🧪Fiber preparation and treatment — can affect surface characteristics and fiber–matrix interaction.
⚙️Fiber–polymer compatibility — influences bonding within the composite.
📊Fiber loading and distribution — affect the material's overall properties.
🏭Processing conditions and composite structure — influence consistency and final performance.

🔬AND THE RESEARCH IS WORTH PAYING ATTENTION TO.
A 2024 life-cycle assessment published in the Journal of Cleaner Production compared a defined coir-fiber-reinforced polypropylene component with a comparable glass-fiber-reinforced polypropylene component.
In that particular study, the coir-based composite showed lower cumulative energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions within the assessed system boundaries.
That is promising evidence.

At CocoHeroBorneo, we believe cocofiber deserves to be explored beyond conventional applications—as a potential raw material for the next generation of natural-fiber composite development.

Southeast Asia's data-centre boom just hit a wall — and it isn't power.

On 19 November, the US Bureau of Industry and Security closed the "remote access" loophole: advanced AI chips now need a US licence to ship to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Data centres anywhere that provide large volumes of compute to China-headquartered firms need a licence — existing arrangements have 90 days to get one. A week later, Nvidia told Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server shipments to the four Southeast Asian countries. The chips stopped before the power did.

Who it hits:

The operators whose tenants are Chinese tech. Asian data centres are now trying to offload excess compute to US buyers. B300 GPU-hour prices have already fallen 7%.

The lenders. Major global and Singapore banks are reviewing their data-centre clients. One major bank is shopping a ~$1bn risk transfer to offload data-centre and infrastructure loan risk. Asia-Pacific data-centre loans have gone from near zero to over $49bn since 2023 — and S&P says even if the rule were reversed tomorrow, lenders will stay cautious.

What it means for power developers in the region:

A data centre with grid connection and no GPUs is stranded capacity — and a power contract is only as bankable as the tenant's chip access.

So underwrite the end user, not just the operator. For lenders, that means the tenant's tenant is now a credit question. The premium now sits with campuses serving US-headquartered hyperscalers, domestic enterprise and sovereign AI — the demand that doesn't need a licence to exist. And build flexibility into the power: grid plus storage that can serve other loads if the tenant's compute gets cut off.

Who is your tenant's tenant?

Why Private Equity Investors Avoid Early Construction Risk in Indonesian Waste-to-Energy: The Post-COD Brownfield Entry Strategy

While institutional private equity and infrastructure funds hold substantial dry powder for Southeast Asia’s energy transition, early-stage greenfield Waste-to-Energy (WtE) projects in Indonesia rarely clear private equity investment committees.

Unlike utility-scale solar or wind—where construction schedules and resource yields are relatively predictable—greenfield WtE developments face acute early-stage risks: multi-year municipal permitting, social opposition (NIMBY), seasonal wet-waste composition shocks, and boiler-commissioning delays. 

Consequently, disciplined institutional equity increasingly adopts a post-Commercial Operation Date (COD) brownfield entry strategy, allowing specialist EPC-led developers and development finance institutions (DFIs) to absorb initial construction and commissioning risk before institutional capital steps in to scale.

From an energy investment origination and enterprise risk governance perspective, post-COD WtE acquisitions achieve institutional financial close only when proven multi-season operating track records, municipal payment-security tracks, and long-term maintenance reserves are verified upfront.

Six core pillars define institutional underwriting for post-COD brownfield WtE acquisitions in Indonesia:

 1. Multi-Season Operating & Calorific Performance Verification: Requiring 12–24 months of audited post-COD operating data across rainy and dry seasons validates true net electrical output, auxiliary fuel burn, and boiler availability against high-moisture tropical waste.

 2. Demonstrated Municipal Tipping Fee (BLPS) & PLN Payment Track Record: Verifying consistent, on-time regional budget (APBD) tipping fee disbursements and PLN Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) settlements—reinforced by Indonesia Infrastructure Guarantee Fund (PII/IIGF) wraps—de-risks cash-flow predictability.

 3. Long-Term O&M Binding & Major-Overhaul Reserve Accounts: Retaining tier-one operators under performance-linked Operation & Maintenance (O&M) contracts alongside fully funded Maintenance Reserve Accounts (MRA) insulates equity yields from unexpected turbine or refractory replacements.

 4. CEMS Emissions Compliance & Leachate Audit Clearance: Confirming uninterrupted Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) records, dioxin/furan stack-test compliance, and zero-discharge leachate performance eliminates latent Ministry KLHK enforcement liabilities.

 5. Debt Refinancing & Yield-Compression Upside: Replacing high-cost construction loans with lower-margin, long-tenor commercial or sustainability-linked project debt post-COD unlocks immediate equity IRR expansion.

 6. Clean Concession Transferability & Zero-Tolerance ABAC Controls: Ensuring seamless municipal change-of-control approvals, unencumbered land/asset titles, and uncompromising ABAC governance protects institutional credit committees.

Thank you CNBC Indonesia & MbakShafinaz Nachiar for hosting me on Monday's Profit Tech a Look. This one means a lot to the wholeSarana team, & I'm grateful for the chance to share what we've been learning on the ground deploying AI across 20 industries in Southeast Asia.

We started Sarana on the tenet that AI should close the productivity delta, rather than feed the usual doom-&-gloom labour-efficiency narrative. After all, when enterprises become more productive, they tend to need more people, not fewer. 

Our job is to give the most precious commodity of all back to the people on the frontlines powering our economy: time. Some numbers that shape our thinking:

• Of the roughly 5% we grow today, about 2.5 points come from capital, 1.6 from labour & only around 1 from productivity (Ministry of Finance)
• For the 8% target, Bank Indonesia estimates productivity's contribution needs to triple, to about 3.6 points a year through 2029
• With an ICOR of around 6, every Rp 1 of extra output still takes about Rp 6 of investment, so capital alone may not carry us there

So the gap has to close through what every working hour produces, & that is where we believe AI earns its place: helping the same people get more done in the same day, & go home on time.

The pressure falls on operators serving Chinese customers, or relying on the latest Nvidia hardware without a US parent.

So Thailand's boom is not stopping. It is splitting.

Truth be told, public speaking has never been my thing, and I usually try to avoid class presentations. I’ve never competed in anything like this before, and taking the stage meant stepping way outside my comfort zone, especially with all the nerves walking up to present.

I’m grateful to come away with 3rd place at the IMechE Speak Out for Engineering (SOfE) National Finals 2026, even though I still have plenty of room to grow.

Congratulations to the champion Rui Qi Lim, and wishing you all the best representing Malaysia at the regional final in Jakarta! Shoutout as well to Archanna Ragunathan, Jocelyn Gresia, Neha Kalakota, and Aiman Hakim . Watching you guys command the stage so effortlessly was honestly inspiring. 👏

Most of all, I want to express my gratitude to theIMechE Sunway Student Chapter , and hats off toShelley Song andVinoshan Nair for hosting such a great and seamless event. From organizing the internal selection to running the competition so smoothly, thank you for all the hard work behind the scenes. A huge thank you as well to Dr.Choon Lih Hoo for his valuable input and guidance, and to my peers at Sunway University for pushing me to go for it.

1,200 Languages, One Chatbot

The complete list of things I can say with confidence in Southeast Asian languages:

* “Thank you” in Thai.
* “Thank you” in Vietnamese.
* “Thank you” in Indonesian.
* “Not spicy, please,” in all of them at once, mostly with my face.
* “The bill, please,” by gesture. This language is understood everywhere from Hanoi to Jakarta, and judging by how fast the bill arrives, it’s a native one.

A short list. But it turns out that for a long time, AI and I were in roughly the same league in this region. At least I never pretended otherwise.

A language that isn’t on the internet

Start with the basics. Large language models learn from the internet. The internet is written mostly in English, then Chinese, then other big languages. Southeast Asia, by the count local developers cite, is home to more than 1,200 languages. Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Malay, Tagalog, Khmer, Lao and Burmese are just the ones with their own countries. Then there’s Javanese, spoken by tens of millions, plus Sundanese, Balinese and Batak. People live, haggle and sing lullabies in them. They don’t write much online.

To a machine, a language that isn’t on the internet doesn’t exist. To the grandmother who speaks it, the internet doesn’t exist. Call it a draw.

The first to treat this as a business problem rather than a cultural one were, interestingly, Chinese. In December 2023, Alibaba’s DAMO Academy released SeaLLMs, 7- and 13-billion-parameter models for Vietnamese, Indonesian, Thai, Malay, Khmer, Lao, Tagalog and Burmese. Analysts were frank about who needed them: Chinese e-commerce and logistics firms entering the region and struggling to hire and keep enough local livestream hosts.

Now that’s an honest product brief. Not “preserve linguistic diversity,” but “we need a salesperson who can say ‘discount’ in Khmer and never asks for a holiday.” Alibaba, remember, owns Lazada in the region. For Lazada, languages aren’t linguistics. They’re revenue.

The most honest motive in tech is commercial. At least it doesn’t pretend to be charity.

Singaporean neutrality

Then there’s Singapore, a country that approaches everything with a budget and a spreadsheet. In December 2023 it launched a national multimodal AI program worth 70 million Singapore dollars. Its flagship is SEA-LION, AI Singapore’s model for regional languages.
